analysis_refs.text:
The next strongest scholarly-book candidates are DOAB/OAPEN, followed by
Wikisource for multilingual editions. They remain researched candidates, not
enabled sources. No paid integration, new reader account or source outreach
was performed. Redis remains deferred for the four existing live paper adapters;
the book catalogs and source research are independent of that setup.

analysis_refs.heading: 10. Progress report and immediate next batch
analysis_refs.text:
The content categories are accepted. The next research cycle uses M1 across all
20 categories and 20 industry tags with the six playbooks. In M2,
prioritize book/education/India opportunities plus US/India public records/maps
and practical industry documentation: DOAB/OAPEN publisher coverage,
national/regional literature catalogs, school textbook bodies, children's
publishers, thesis repositories, audiobook catalogs, official civic/property
catalogs, geological data and agriculture/construction/manufacturing/logistics
guidance. Recheck existing source
freshness first; new names do not solve an expired catalog or a three-item pilot.

analysis_refs.heading: Phase B — initial coverage
analysis_refs.text: Add Open Textbook Library, DOAJ and arXiv; OpenAlex after key/budget verification. Then DOAB/OAPEN imports and optional Unpaywall resolver with real contact email. Keep Google/Open Library enrichment bounded.

analysis_refs.heading: C04. Textbooks and scholarly books/chapters
analysis_refs.text:
**Best starting points.** [DOAB metadata](https://doabooks.org/en/librarians/doab-metadata)
documents CC0 exports and OAI-PMH, including selective publisher/subject exports.
Use publisher identities to discover origins and verify their actual OA subsets.
[Open Textbook Library discovery](https://open.umn.edu/opentextbooks/discovery)
documents MARC/CSV, JSON resources and change feeds. Follow textbook publisher and
institution links into university presses and open-education programs. These
catalogs expose different kinds of books; keep textbooks, monographs and chapters
distinct even when the same publisher supplies all three.

analysis_refs.heading: C04. Textbooks and scholarly books/chapters
analysis_refs.text:
**Search process.** Enumerate publisher-origin candidates from approved metadata
exports by discipline, language and geography; inspect batches of 25 distinct
publishers. Search `"{university press}" "open access books"`,
`"{subject}" "open textbook" "{country}"`, and
`site:{education-body-domain} (textbook OR publication) (catalog OR download)`.
Follow open-education network members into their own catalogs and compare against
DOAB/OTL holdings. To approach 100, add qualified publisher catalogs across
disciplines, not 100 series from one press. Record the fraction actually covered
by the aggregator; a few OA titles never imply a wholly free publisher catalog.

analysis_refs.heading: C04. Textbooks and scholarly books/chapters
analysis_refs.text:
**Retrieval to investigate.** Prefer DOAB/OTL-origin mapping and official exports
before custom publisher connectors. OAI-PMH needs an import and local keyword
index; it is not a topic-search API. Per-book licenses and destinations remain
separate from the metadata feed license. Verify withdrawn records, corrected
editions and bounded refresh costs without provisioning a hosted database.

analysis_refs.heading: C04. Textbooks and scholarly books/chapters
analysis_refs.text:
**First ten leads:** four Indian educational publishers/institutions, four new
publishers represented in DOAB/OTL, and two independently maintained catalogs from
underrepresented regions. Deep-review a publisher represented by an export and
an India school-text catalog to compare integration and refresh effort.

analysis_refs.heading: Evidence boundaries and next handoff
analysis_refs.text:
Documentation opens succeeded for IBBY, Parag, Book Dash, Gutenberg, OTL, DOAB,
Project Madurai, LibriVox, DAISY and NLS during this planning review. The research
tool returned HTTP 402 for StoryWeaver's open-content page, 502 for NCERT's
textbook page and 403 for DPLA's API page. Sugamya redirected to its current domain
but exposed no readable content to the tool. These observations establish neither
payment requirements nor source-wide outages. No credentials, source accounts,
outreach, bulk harvests or live query qualification probes were performed.

analysis_refs.heading: What the original checks established
analysis_refs.text: Structured responses were obtained from Google Books (using the configured key), Open Library, Internet Archive, DOAJ, OpenAlex, Crossref, arXiv, Europe PMC, CORE, Zenodo, HAL, Wikisource, Library of Congress, and LibriVox. Gutenberg RDF and DOAB record/harvesting responses also worked. OAPEN's OAI service identification worked; a record import was not exercised.

analysis_refs.heading: What the original checks established
analysis_refs.text:
- An Open Library work returned `ebook_access: public` alongside many Internet Archive identifiers. That does not identify which edition is freely readable.
- A HAL hit had a record URL and DOI but no `fileMain_s`: a repository hit is not necessarily full text.
- Zenodo returned a dataset; item-type filtering is essential.
- DOAJ supplied an older HTTP publisher URL; metadata alone does not prove the destination still works.
- Semantic Scholar returned **429**, and Gutendex timed out. Those checks do not establish general service availability.
- Some documentation URLs moved; corrected DOAB/OAPEN URLs appear in the catalog. Some sites returned only a JavaScript shell. NCERT/ERIC/OER Commons could not be fully inspected.

analysis_refs.heading: Technical recovery continuation G — 6 November 2026
analysis_refs.text:
- **NQR:** a single retry of the previously failed Mine Electrician query succeeded after roughly 90 minutes of backoff. It used the same advertised public browser form and identity. All ten current keyword cases now pass; the earlier 403 and advanced-form 500 remain saved. Availability is intermittent and no qualification files were fetched.
- **NCERT:** CIET's current ePathshala site links its actual textbook selector through a public iframe. Its published metadata contains 427 active selector rows and 421 unambiguous searchable records after repeated contexts, one unresolved subject selector and one conflicting title/native-code mapping are handled explicitly. Ten title/class searches, exact native-code and empty controls pass. Six commented metadata blocks remain inactive historical findings; no book bodies were downloaded. The footer license URL returned404, so metadata queryability does not establish reuse rights or full reading access.
- **Gallica:** BnF documents a separate public SPARQL service whose bibliographic editions link to native Gallica digital ARKs. Ten exact literal-title queries pass through that service. The parser was corrected to accept its legacy typed-literal XSD-string representation; failed attempts remain saved. Direct Gallica SRU and general-catalog restrictions are unchanged. This is a linked-data subset, not whole-Gallica keyword or full-text search.
- **SciELO:** the operator developer index and REST client document a separate anonymous ArticleMeta service. Ten native article-PID lookups now return matching Brazil-collection metadata with `body=false`. Original article title markup, language variants, journal identity, processing/publication dates and content URLs are kept separate. No article bodies were requested, and no linked content was fetched. This does not prove upstream keyword or whole-network search. The old documentation link returned404; network-search403 and regional OAI503 remain preserved.
- **Chicago zoning:** the published schema endpoint still returned503 after a multi-hour backoff. Current SODA2.1 documentation alone does not establish working dataset access. No underlying zoning query was sent after the failure.
- **OER Commons:** current operator help documents anonymous homepage search, but the primary site's policy still returns403. No homepage/search request or staging/private API workaround was sent.
- **Gutendex:** native8746 recovered after nearly two hours of backoff, but the next saved native10836 query returned503. Two of ten current native cases pass; the connector remains blocked. No broad-search retry followed that503. Unknown CLI case IDs now fail before any network dispatch, preventing silent no-op attempts.
- **DOAB and India Code:** one policy-only retry each after more than four and three hours of backoff, respectively, still timed out. No target catalog request was sent. Further timed retries are deferred until16:00UTC unless a useful recovery signal arrives.
- **DIKSHA:** the current homepage exposes14 native featured quiz links. Ten links for five topics have consistent published banner/topic/language labels and pass local metadata queries plus an empty control. Four links in two conflicting or unreviewed banner groups are quarantined. These are language variants, not extra origins. The main Library remains login-gated, and the teacher-page Search Course text is an instructional heading, not a guest search form. No course/quiz content or account flow was requested.
- **NSDC:** current public sitemap navigation revealed its sector-skills report search. Ten title-word queries and an empty-result control pass. Duplicate responsive inputs and a Search button that changes into an icon required browser-selector corrections; all failed attempts remain saved. The same operator's report-file URLs identify results without downloading PDFs. The original occupational-standards/model-curriculum catalog remains unverified and is explicitly outside this recovered subset. No staging API, direct backend replay or account flow was used.

analysis_refs.heading: Blocker investigation
analysis_refs.text:
- **FDIC Money Smart:** official documentation points to a separate catalog service. Its policy endpoint returned503, so no catalog/product query was sent. Wait for recovery; next timed check no earlier than16:00UTC without a new service signal.
- **LINCS:** API/RSS documentation searches did not establish a supported new interface. Unrelated third-party feeds, staging sites and host switching are not adopted as alternatives. CERT-In was subsequently recovered through its public metadata list after manual policy diagnosis.
- **Tamil Nadu land records:** the separate map-only Survey and Settlement service has policy503. No map/parcel/owner query was sent; wait until16:00UTC or a concrete recovery signal.
- **DOAB/OAPEN:** the officially documented Penn State export dataset pages are accessible, but their file routes return a traffic-control/Turnstile challenge. HTTP200 is not a metadata success. No files or signed-token alternatives were fetched after recognizing the challenge. OAPEN lists an October2026 snapshot; DOAB still lists May2024 with updates paused. A provider-permitted or owner-supplied export could unblock local metadata search.
- **NHM:** the exact published policy redirect timed out; no catalog request. **CMDA:** another policy503 after more than4hours backoff, with upstream connection timeout. **Let’s Read:** the response identifies a login-page app shell; no hidden API or login attempted.

analysis_refs.heading: Technical recovery K — owner paused, 6 November 2026
analysis_refs.text: DOAB and OAPEN each now have ten passing live title queries through OpenAlex’s documented repository-location index. Native OAI identifiers remain separate from OpenAlex work IDs; the old OAPEN source alias resolves to canonicalS4306402535. Queries use the canonical source plus book and reported-open-access filters, then literal title-token checks over the first5 results. One title returns two distinct OAPEN records; neither is merged.
